t: Galicia closes public input on its new General Gaming Regulation
d: The period for suggestions on Galicia's draft General Gaming Regulation closed on 26 October with 31 suggestions received. The decree is still pending approval.
b: The regional government of Galicia closed the period for public suggestions on its draft decree approving a new General Gaming Regulation on 26 October 2026.
The region's transparency portal records 31 suggestions received. The suggestion period opened on 24 July 2026. The procedure itself started on 9 February 2026.
The draft is handled by the regional Ministry of Finance and Public Administration, through its Technical General Secretariat and Treasury. Its status is listed as pending approval.
src: Xunta de Galicia Transparency Portal, draft General Gaming Regulation

t: Dutch online gambling accounts rise to 1.48 million in the first half of 2026
d: The Dutch gambling regulator KSA published its half-year monitoring report on online gambling for the first half of 2026. The number of online accounts rose and the share of spending at licensed sites went up.
b: The KSA published its half-year monitoring report on online gambling on 29 October 2026. It covers the first half of 2026 and tracks player losses, account numbers and channelisation.

Online accounts rose to 1.48 million, from 1.38 million half a year earlier. The KSA says the rise may partly reflect the men's World Cup, which started in June, or players opening more accounts to get around per-account deposit limits.

Around 490,000 people gamble online in a typical month, and about 820,000 played online at some point in the half year. About 94% of players gamble only with licensed operators. Measured by gross gaming revenue, channelisation rose from 54% in the second half of 2025 to an estimated 59%.
The KSA also cites treatment data showing 14% more people in care for gambling addiction in 2025 than in 2024.
src: Kansspelautoriteit, Stand van zaken Nederlandse gokmarkt 2025 - 2026, 29 Oct 2026

t: Colombian bill seeks to keep minors away from online gambling
d: A group of members of Colombia's Chamber of Representatives filed bill 419/2026C on 1 October. It sets responsible play rules for online games of chance and aims to stop children and teenagers from playing.
b: Bill 419/2026C was filed in the Chamber of Representatives on 1 October 2026. It was published in Gaceta 1497 of 2026.
The bill sets prevention, information, control and responsible play measures for games of chance offered over the internet. One stated aim is to prevent children and adolescents from taking part.
It also seeks to protect mental health and consumer rights, and to reduce the social, family and economic harm of problem gambling.
The bill is with the Sixth Constitutional Committee for its first debate in the 2026-2027 session.

t: IAGR recognises Peru's progress on gambling regulation after Lima conference
d: Peru hosted the International Association of Gaming Regulators annual conference in Lima from 19 to 22 October 2026. The trade and tourism ministry said the association recognised Peru's progress in regulating gambling.
b: Lima hosted the annual conference of the International Association of Gaming Regulators (IAGR) from 19 to 22 October 2026. About 200 representatives of regulators and public bodies took part. Delegations came from Austria, Croatia, Latvia, Poland, Slovenia, the Czech Republic, China, Gibraltar, Finland, the Netherlands, the United States, Canada and other countries.
This was the second time Peru hosted the conference. The first was ten years earlier.

Sessions covered the growth of online betting, the fight against illegal operators, the integrity of sports betting, strategies against illegal gambling in Latin America, Africa and Europe, and the use of data to prevent money laundering.

The Ministry of Foreign Trade and Tourism (MINCETUR), which regulates casinos, slot machines and remote gaming and betting, said the IAGR recognised Peru's progress in gambling regulation. The announcement did not list the specific measures recognised.
src: Andina, Mincetur: reconocen avances del Peru en regulacion de juegos de azar, 26 Oct 2026

t: Namibia's gambling board extends deadline for monitoring and licensing system tenders
d: The Gambling Board of Namibia moved the closing date for two technology tenders from 29 October to 5 November 2026.
b: The Gambling Board of Namibia has extended the closing date for two technology tenders. Public Notice 003 of 2026, issued on 9 October, moves the submission deadline from 29 October 2026 at 11:00 to 5 November 2026 at 11:00. The board says all other terms stay the same.

Tender SC/RP/GBN-01/2026 covers the supply, deployment and maintenance of a central electronic monitoring system. Tender SC/RP/GBN-02/2026 covers an automated licensing, workflow and document management system, with a 60-month assignment period.
The board issued clarifications on the first tender on 6 October and on the second on 20 October.
src: Gambling Board of Namibia, Procurement page, Public Notice 003 of 2026, 9 Oct 2026

t: South Africa's National Gambling Board tenders a study on problem gambling
d: The National Gambling Board sought bids for research on how common gambling and problem gambling are in South Africa. Bids closed on 27 October 2026.
b: The National Gambling Board (NGB) published tender NGB 002(2026/2027), a request for proposals for research to determine the prevalence of gambling and problem gambling in South Africa.
Bids closed on 27 October 2026. On 23 October the board issued an erratum together with answers to questions from bidders.
The tender documents are on the procurement notices page of the NGB website.

t: Ghana's National Lottery Authority resumes dividends with GH¢10 million
d: Ghana's National Lottery Authority handed a GH¢10 million dividend to the government on 2 October. Its dividend payments had stopped after 2017.
b: The board and management of the National Lottery Authority (NLA) presented a GH¢10 million dividend to the finance minister on 2 October 2026.
The NLA used to pay dividends every year, but payments stopped after 2017. The ministry described the payment as a resumption.

The ministry said it is reviewing, with the NLA and the Attorney-General, agreements that limited the authority's returns to the state. The finance minister called the payment a good step but said taxpayers deserve more.
